title: If it happens
takeaway: If it happens, move what is left to a new wallet, revoke and report, and never pay anyone who promises to get your funds back.

cards.title: Breathe, then act
cards.body: Scammers are professionals. Anyone can be fooled. Acting fast is what matters. Your dragons just left your wallet. Minutes later, the helpers arrive in your DMs. Some of them are the next scam.

seg.label: Sympathy
seg.why: Kind words are not the problem.

seg.t: Send 0.05 ETH to your old wallet
seg.label: Send ETH to a swept wallet
seg.why: A sweeper bot takes it instantly.

seg.label: Rushed fix
seg.why: Panic helps scammers. Follow the steps.

cards.title: Step 1: Which case are you in?
cards.body: Use a clean device, not the one that was attacked. If many assets or chains are gone, including ETH, your seed phrase or key leaked. If assets went out through one contract, it was an approval or a signature. The next step depends on your case.

cards.title: Steps 2 and 3: Revoke, or move out
cards.body: Approval or signature: revoke that spender on revoke.cash now. Key or seed leak: treat the wallet as lost. Make a new wallet on a clean device, without reusing a cloud login. Move what is left. Never send ETH to a wallet you think is swept. For more than about $1,000 stuck, contact the Flashbots Whitehat Hotline.

cards.title: Steps 4 to 6: Lock down, ignore, report
cards.body: Stop using the old wallet. Protect your email, X and Discord with an authenticator app or passkey. Ignore every recovery helper: stolen funds cannot be pulled back on chain. Report it to Chainabuse, the police or IC3, the exchange if funds went to one, and the team through the official Discord ticket only, never a DM.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: A recovery service replies to your post. Tap each red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting is not the problem.

seg.t: We traced your dragons and can recover 100%.
seg.label: Guaranteed recovery
seg.why: Stolen funds cannot be pulled back on chain.

seg.label: Upfront fee
seg.why: Recovery scams always ask for fees first.

questions.stem: Your ETH, tokens and NFTs all left on two chains within minutes. Which case is this most likely?
options: Your seed phrase or key leaked
One bad approval you gave last week
A wallet display bug after an update
A network delay that will fix itself
questions.why: Many assets across chains, including ETH, points to a leaked seed or key. Treat that wallet as lost.

questions.stem: Only your USDC left, through one contract you approved yesterday. What do you do first?
options: Revoke that spender on revoke.cash now
Make a new seed phrase first
Wait a day to see what happens
Disconnect the site to stop the contract
questions.why: Assets gone through one contract means an approval or signature. Revoke that spender now so it cannot take more.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Sympathy
seg.why: Kind words are not the problem.

seg.t: I will send ETH for gas to your old wallet
seg.label: Gas into a swept wallet
seg.why: A sweeper bot takes incoming ETH instantly.

seg.label: Rush
seg.why: Panic helps sweepers. Follow the steps.

questions.why: Never send ETH to a wallet you think is swept. A sweeper bot takes it. For more than about $1,000 stuck, contact the Flashbots Whitehat Hotline.

questions.stem: Your old wallet is swept, but NFTs worth about $3,000 are still stuck there. Who can help?
options: The Flashbots Whitehat Hotline, through its own site
A recovery agent who DMed you with proof
A rescue bot that someone shares in chat
A team admin who messages you first
questions.why: For more than about $1,000 stuck, the Flashbots Whitehat Hotline may help. Contact it only through its own site.

questions.stem: After a leak you set up a new wallet. How do you set it up?
options: A clean device, and no reused cloud login
On the old device, after a full restart
On the old device, with a new password
By restoring it from your old seed phrase
questions.why: Make the new wallet on a clean device and do not reuse a cloud login tied to the old one.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Noticed your post
seg.why: Seeing your post is not the problem.

seg.label: Guaranteed recovery
seg.why: No one can guarantee getting stolen crypto back.

seg.label: Seed request
seg.why: Never share your seed phrase with anyone.

questions.why: Guaranteed recovery, an upfront fee and a seed request are the recovery scam pattern. Stop and do not pay.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Mentions your ticket
seg.why: Scammers watch for tickets, so this proves nothing.

seg.t: I am team support in DMs.
seg.label: Support in DMs
seg.why: The team answers only inside the ticket.

seg.t: Send your seed to secure the wallet.
seg.label: Seed request
seg.why: Nobody real asks for your seed.

questions.why: The team replies only inside the official Discord ticket, never by DM, and never asks for your seed phrase.

questions.stem: A blockchain investigator offers to freeze the thief's wallet if you pay a fee first. What do you do?
options: Ignore them and do not pay anything
Pay the fee, freezing a wallet is possible
Pay half now and half after the freeze
Give them wallet access instead of a fee
questions.why: Private helpers cannot reverse transfers on chain. Rare freezes come from exchanges or police, never from strangers charging fees.

questions.stem: You want to tell the Pocket Dragons team what happened. How do you do it?
options: Open a ticket in the official Discord
Reply to the support DM that found you
Post your wallet details in the main chat
DM the first admin who answers you
questions.why: Tell the team through the official Discord ticket only. Anyone who DMs you as support is a scammer.

questions.stem: Your funds are moved and safe. Where do you report the scam address?
options: Chainabuse, plus the police or IC3
Nowhere, reports never get funds back
A recovery service that DMs you
Only in a public post to warn others
questions.why: Report to Chainabuse to warn others, and to the police or IC3. Tell the exchange too if funds went to one.

sources.label: revoke.cash: What to do when scammed
MetaMask Support: I have been hacked
IC3 (United States; elsewhere use your local police cybercrime unit)
